title: Game and interactive
covers: Browser and Godot games, interactive demos, quizzes and playful experiences someone plays rather than reads.

stakeholders.who: A first-time player on the device the game targets
cares_about: knowing what to do within seconds
would_notice: no idea what the goal or the controls are
a frozen screen with no way out
controls cut off on a phone

stakeholders.who: A player who comes back or plays again
cares_about: their progress or high score kept
a restart that really starts fresh
would_notice: the high score gone after a reload
the game running faster, or sounds doubling, after a restart

stakeholders.who: A QA tester playing a full session with DevTools open
cares_about: no errors over a long session
would_notice: red console errors after a few minutes
stutter when many objects are on screen

first_ten_seconds: Look at the start screen for ten seconds: can you tell the goal and the controls?
Press the first key or tap: does something respond at once?
On a phone-sized viewport: is anything cut off or too small to touch?

checks.claim: Within the first screen the player can tell the goal and the controls, from the screen itself or a short prompt.
checks.how_to_inspect: Show the start screen to someone (or look at it yourself, cold) for ten seconds and ask what the goal and controls are.
checks.evidence_required: The start-screen screenshot and the answer given.

source.rationale: A player who cannot tell the goal or controls in the first seconds leaves; no later polish wins them back.

checks.claim: The loop completes: start, play, win AND lose are both reachable, and restart works from each.
checks.how_to_inspect: Play (or drive with browser automation) to a win and to a loss, and restart from each end screen.
checks.evidence_required: Screenshots or a recording of win, lose and restart.

source.quote: reaching a win and a lose condition and a working restart

checks.claim: There is no state the player cannot leave: pause and resume work and input never stops responding.
checks.how_to_inspect: Try to break it: pause during a transition, die during a level change, mash keys, switch tabs and come back.
checks.evidence_required: The list of attempts and what happened in each.

checks.claim: The game scales or letterboxes at phone and desktop sizes with no cut-off controls or HUD, or it clearly says it is desktop-only.
checks.how_to_inspect: Screenshot the play screen at a phone size and at a desktop size, in both orientations on the phone.

source.quote: The canvas scales/letterboxes correctly at mobile and desktop sizes with no cut-off UI

checks.claim: Every declared input works (keyboard, mouse, touch as promised), and touch controls are big enough to hit on a phone.
checks.how_to_inspect: Play one round with each declared input method, the touch round on a phone-sized viewport.
checks.evidence_required: A note per input method with what was tested.

checks.claim: Every player action gets immediate feedback (sound, motion or a visual change), and scoring or damage is visible.
checks.how_to_inspect: Perform each action once and note what the player sees or hears in response.
checks.evidence_required: The action list with the feedback for each.

checks.claim: A new player can win the first level, with no instant death or unwinnable start.
checks.how_to_inspect: Play the first level as a beginner would, three times, without using knowledge of the code.
checks.evidence_required: The outcome of the three tries.

source.rationale: Difficulty spikes in the first minute are the most common reason testers stop playing.

checks.claim: Score, lives, timers and menus are readable at phone size and never cover the play area.
checks.how_to_inspect: Look at the HUD in the phone-size screenshot at real size.
checks.evidence_required: The phone-size screenshot with the HUD noted.

source.rationale: A HUD designed at desktop size becomes unreadable, or blocks the action, on a phone.

checks.claim: Sound can be muted, does not blast on load, and starts only after a user gesture where browsers require it.
checks.how_to_inspect: Load the game with sound on and check the volume at start and the mute control.
checks.evidence_required: A note on start volume and the mute control (N/A for a silent game).

source.rationale: Unexpected loud audio makes players close the tab, and browsers block autoplay anyway.

checks.claim: Saves and high scores, when promised, persist and restore after a reload.
checks.how_to_inspect: Set a score or save, reload the page, and check it is restored.
checks.evidence_required: Before and after screenshots (N/A when nothing persistent was promised).

source.quote: Save/load / high-scores (if promised) persist and restore across reloads.

checks.claim: A restart resets everything: no doubled speed, double-fired sounds or leftover timers and listeners.
checks.how_to_inspect: Restart five times in a row and watch speed, sound and the listener count in DevTools.
checks.evidence_required: A note on the fifth run compared with the first.

source.quote: listeners/timers/audio cleaned up on restart (no leak, no double-fire)

checks.claim: A full session of several minutes shows zero console errors and a steady frame rate.
checks.how_to_inspect: Play for at least five minutes with the console and the performance monitor open.
checks.evidence_required: The console capture and the frame-rate reading.

source.quote: Zero console errors across a full session

common_sloppy_defects.symptom: a start screen with a title and a Play button, and no hint of goal or controls
after a few restarts the game runs faster and every sound plays twice
dying during a level transition leaves a black screen with no way back
touch does nothing, or the controls sit outside the phone screen
the promised high score resets to 0 after a reload
